finalText:
Migration finished. All 36 remaining `db.query(sql, params)` call sites across 12 files are now `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |

All files pass `node --check`. There's no package.json or test suite in the repo, so that's the only verification available.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — the last two `db.query` calls in the tree. The file header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local changes silently lost. Patching it would be undone by the next upgrade, so this needs either an upstream fix or a wrapper on your side. Flagging it rather than editing.
- **`cache.query(...)`** (~20 sites) — different object, unrelated API, not part of this migration.

`db.query` itself is still defined in `lib/db.js:13` with a `@deprecated` tag. Once vendor is resolved you can delete it; I left it in place since the vendored adapter still calls it.
